admissions.reproduction: GNU Make executes printf '%s' 'before\u2028after' unchanged; the adapter truncates after before. A comment with U+2028 followed by SHELL=python3 makes the adapter skip shell analysis although native Make still uses /bin/sh.
admissions.gap: str.splitlines treats literal non-LF separator data as Make line boundaries.
admissions.harm: Commands are truncated, diagnostics use wrong physical lines, and fake assignments in comments can bypass shell analysis.
admissions.invalidStateVersusPreference: Project exactly the physical Make recipe; keep existing syntax, shells and formatting policy.
admissions.smallestFix: Split Make input only at LF, retaining internal carriage returns and removing a terminal CR for native CRLF lines.

admissions.reproduction: Both randomly selected PostgreSQL rules build the same docstring constant-id set for a shared PythonFileContext; no-offset-pagination duplicates the same owner test.
admissions.gap: Three copies repeat identical indexed AST owner classification per file.
admissions.harm: Repeated deterministic work and duplicated exclusions can drift.
admissions.invalidStateVersusPreference: Implementation-only consolidation, requiring unchanged findings in both rule orders and standalone contexts.
admissions.smallestFix: One lazy immutable docstring_node_ids fact per file context, used by all three existing callers.

reproductionCommands: code-standards --root . maintain rules changes --before origin/main --after HEAD
limitations: This is a reproducible machine-assisted source/test review with native examples. Deep manual analysis and adversarial probes focus on admitted candidates; it is not exhaustive manual review of every selected rule.
300 draws cover 197 distinct rules. Repeated selections reuse evidence and are not independent semantic coverage.
Native case counts can contain equivalent contracts; counts do not imply independent coverage.
Only already-local repositories were scanned; Python selection takes the first 250 sorted eligible tracked paths per root, rather than an unbiased whole-repository sample.
The unseeded Python corpus has zero findings; unchanged zeros are not correctness evidence. Twelve separately pinned seeded files establish positive and negative contracts.

A private inventory-only root advanced during the run. It has no selected native shell or Python files, so it is outside the evaluated native source set; no evaluated revision or digest was refreshed.
One pre-existing native formatter failure remains in the shell corpus. Aggregate native ShellCheck and formatter findings are unchanged.

The initial SC2015 probe used printf, which native ShellCheck treats as a low-risk branch. The final probe uses a fallible command and proves existing upstream ownership; this was a fixture correction, not a linter defect.
Make parses recipes using LF and native CRLF handling; returned finding anchors use canonical SourceDocument editor coordinates when literal carriage returns are present.

The shared-fact benchmark measures three SQL rules on one 74,755-byte fixture. Warm repeated fact access is not ordinary full-file speed; combined median gain is fixture-specific. Cold baseline namespace loader overhead and small memory differences are observational.
Private identities, source pins, paths, hashes, snippets and finding tuples remain in owner-readable overlays; this report exposes only public rule data and redacted aggregates.

Make corpus comparison runs both exact baseline and candidate projections in each fresh per-root process; it does not execute private recipes. Full serialized ExecutionBlock tuples and failure outcomes are equal across 73 pinned files.
The Make corpus includes tracked .mk inputs that retain the existing empty-projection routing; 73 input files is not a claim that every input yields an executable block.
